name: Spotify
payout_model: Pro-rata pool: about two-thirds of revenue to rights holders, split about 4/5 recordings and 1/5 publishing. A track needs 1,000+ streams a year to earn.
our_data: Measured: monthly listeners, streams per song (kworb.net)

name: Apple Music
payout_model: Pro-rata. Apple says it pays 52% of subscription revenue to labels and averages $0.01 per play including publishing (2020, individual plans).
our_data: No play counts published. Estimated from Spotify by market share

name: YouTube (videos and YouTube Music)
payout_model: Ad revenue share plus YouTube Music subscriptions; Content ID pays on fan uploads too. YouTube paid the music industry over $8bn in Jul 2024-Jun 2025. Per official-video view: about $0.60-1.50 per 1,000 from ads; $4.80 is the blended figure with YouTube Music subscriptions (Duetti 2024).

name: Amazon Music
payout_model: Pro-rata; the Prime bundle lifts the per-stream figure.
our_data: No play counts published. Estimated from Spotify by market share

name: Deezer
payout_model: Artist-centric since 2023: double weight for professional artists (1,000+ streams a month from 500+ listeners) and for streams fans seek out.

name: TIDAL
payout_model: Pro-rata; direct artist payouts ended in 2023. Small share of listening.

name: SoundCloud
payout_model: Fan-powered royalties: each listener's money goes only to the artists that listener played. No published rate.
our_data: No open API for new apps; no reliable public figures

name: Audiomack
payout_model: AMP programme, reported 50/50 ad-revenue split. Strong in hip-hop and Afrobeats.

name: TikTok
payout_model: Blanket licences with labels and distributors; pays on share of video creations, not per view. Not modelled per view.

name: Instagram and Facebook
payout_model: Blanket licences with labels (UMG renewed 2024, terms undisclosed). No per-use rate.

name: Other services (Tencent, NetEase, Pandora, regional)
payout_model: Mostly outside the US hip-hop audience; Pandora is US radio-style.
